commitResults.messageTitle: Adds support for read & save files
Extract task collection responsibilities into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Move task capacity, numbering, mutation, and status-sorting logic out of Caesar so the command loop can coordinate higher-level behavior without owning the collection. Preserve task display, persistence, and rollback behavior while introducing a defensive task-list boundary.

Move task-file creation, loading, serialization, deserialization, and saving out of Caesar. Keep user-facing file creation feedback in Caesar, preserve the legacy loading helper, and centralize persistence behind a Storage instance.

Move command splitting, argument validation, date conversion, deadline and event construction, and parser error messages out of Caesar. Restore Caesar as the command coordinator while retaining the public CommandType API for compatibility.

Move console input, welcome and farewell messages, task display, error reporting, and task-operation feedback out of Caesar. Keep Caesar focused on coordinating Parser, Storage, TaskList, and the application loop while preserving existing command-line behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor Caesar into an instance-based application
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce Caesar fields for Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList, load dependencies through a constructor, and move the command loop into run(). Keep the default main entry point and existing command-line behavior while preparing the application for command object extraction.

Add an abstract Command contract with execute and isExit methods, and migrate the bye branch to ExitCommand. This establishes the stretch-goal command architecture incrementally while preserving the existing parser, task operations, UI output, and persistence behavior.

Move ordinary and status-sorted list behavior into a concrete Command implementation. Caesar now dispatches the list operation through the command execution contract while preserving UI output, sorting behavior, and persistence.

Move the shared add, save, rollback, and success-feedback workflow into AddCommand for todo, deadline, and event tasks. Caesar now delegates task creation results to an executable command while preserving validation and persistence behavior.

Move task-number deletion, persistence, rollback, and success feedback into DeleteCommand. Caesar now delegates delete execution through the command abstraction while preserving one-based validation and task ordering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task status changes into commands
commitResults.messageBody: Move mark and unmark mutations, persistence rollback, and UI feedback into separate MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand classes. Caesar now dispatches both status operations through the command execution contract.

Make Parser construct concrete Command objects for every supported command and simplify Caesar.run() to read, parse, execute, and check isExit(). Remove the remaining command switch from Caesar while preserving validation, UI output, persistence, and compatibility parsing.

Complete the package reorganization by adding declarations that match each source folder and importing cross-package dependencies. Keep Caesar as the application entry point, separate command, parser, storage, task, UI, and exception packages, and preserve the packaged runtime behavior.
